comments.author: avar
comments.story: Larry Page is pouring millions into flying cars
comments.why: Quadcopter can fly with only three rotors
comments.text: The Ehang 184 has 8 propellers, two for each of the four quad points. I'd assume the reason is safety, that it can limp to the ground with just 7. You're wrong about a quadcopter not being able to fly with 3 rotors, see this video: [VIDEO] That looks like it would be quite a ride with a human on-board, but would probably suck less than crashing.

comments.author: FatalLogic
comments.story: Damage Recovery Algorithm Could Make All Robots Unstoppable
comments.why: Quadcopter recovers from losing one rotor by spinning
comments.text: I wonder if the algorithm could be applied to flying robots or other flying vehicles? If there was sufficient height maybe? It reminds me of this quadcopter drone recovering from the loss of 1 rotor, [VIDEO] Although the drone in that video uses a pre-computed strategy, I think, not a general experiment and learning approach. And it recovers by spinning around on its axis, which saves the drone, and the environment, from further damage, but makes the damaged drone useless for most applications.
